newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's vehicle production rises in September.
newsitem.headline: Japan's vehicle production rises in September.

text.p: A weaker yen and the launch of several new models boosted vehicle production in Japan in September.

Industry sources said overall domestic vehicle production for the month was likely to show a rise of about seven percent from a year earlier to some 923,000 units, after a 2.1 percent decline in August.
Official figures will be announced by the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association next week.

Japan's biggest carmaker Toyota Motor announced on Friday that its domestic production rose 18.6 percent from a year earlier to 302,621 in September. This was due to strong domestic demand for new models such as its "Mark II" luxury sedan series and Ipsum multi-purpose compact minivan, and higher exports helped by weaker yen.
However Nissan Motor, Japan's second-biggest maker, said its domestic output fell 7.5 percent from a year earlier to 146,423 in September.
It said this was partly due to production adjustment as the "new model effect" for sedan models such as Cedric, Gloria, Cefiro and Primera wore off.
It said its domestic sales rose 1.3 percent to 110,500 units due to good demand for its recreational models, and exports rose three percent to 54,992, reflecting good sales in North America.

Honda Motor's domestic production soared 27.3 percent from a year earlier to 100,734 in September, reflecting strong domestic demand for its Step Wagon, CR-V, Accord Wagon and Orthia models, and an increase in exports of Civics to North America.
Mitsubishi Motors' September domestic vehicle output rose 0.9 percent to 114,364 units, but its domestic sales fell 1.1 percent to 76,885.
Exports rose 21.2 percent to 47,247, reflecting a recovery in its sales in North America, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Mazda Motor said its September domestic production rose 5.6 percent from a year earlier to 67,104. It said this was helped by strong domestic demand for its new Demio compact wagon model.

Mazda's domestic sales for the month fell 5.4 percent against last year to 35,051 units, mainly due to slow demand for its trucks and 660cc minivehicles. Its vehicle exports fell 9.6 percent to 43,226 due to slow demand in North America and Europe.
Spokesman for the five big carmakers said the firms were hoping to achieve their annual sales target through sales of new models.
Japanese makers have introduced a total of 20 new models since April.
